document.description: PP_0075 is a multi-pass SLC26A/SulP-family membrane transporter with a cytoplasmic STAS domain. review.summary: The multi-pass architecture supports membrane localization; the specific membrane is the cytoplasmic (plasma) membrane.
review.reason: Membrane is correct but general. Q88RQ4 has nine predicted transmembrane helices and an SLC26A/SulP transport domain, and a Gram-negative bacterium has no internal membrane system in which a multi-pass secondary transporter would reside; the outer membrane holds beta-barrel rather than alpha-helical proteins. The cytoplasmic (inner) membrane, GO:0005886 plasma membrane, is therefore the supported location.

document.description: PP_0076 is a signal-peptide-bearing periplasmic substrate-binding protein in the choline/glycine-betaine transporter binding-protein family. Its physiological ligand and membrane-transport partner are unresolved; current evidence does not establish an ABC complex or direct transmembrane transporter activity for this soluble protein.

review.summary: Transport of a quaternary ammonium compound is supported at family level, but the choline-specific cargo is not.
review.reason: The InterPro2GO mapping transfers choline transport from the choline-transporter substrate-binding family. The OpuAC-type binding-protein domain is shared by binding proteins for several quaternary ammonium compatible solutes, and PP_0076 sits beside the choline sulfatase gene in a locus induced by choline-O-sulfate in a second Pseudomonas, so its cargo could be choline-O-sulfate, choline or a related compound. No target-specific study resolves this. The supported claim is the class-level parent quaternary ammonium group transport (GO:0015697), whose definition covers any compound derived from ammonium by replacement of all four hydrogens with organic groups; choline and choline-O-sulfate both qualify.

review.summary: Exact choline binding is not established; binding of a quaternary ammonium ligand is the supported generalization.
review.reason: The term is a family-based inference. Neither direct ligand-binding data nor target-specific genetics distinguishes choline from choline-O-sulfate or another quaternary ammonium solute for PP_0076. GO:0050997 quaternary ammonium group binding is defined as "Binding to a quaternary ammonium group, including glycine betaine, choline, carnitine and proline" and is the claim the OpuAC-type binding domain supports without committing to a ligand. This is a lateral generalization, not a parent: in GO, GO:0033265 choline binding is_a GO:0043169 cation binding (is_a ion binding, is_a binding), while GO:0050997 is_a GO:0036094 small molecule binding; neither term subsumes the other. Comparator: the KT2440 paralog CaiX (Q88R30, also NCBIfam TIGR03414 ABC_choline_bnd) is reviewed in this repository as the L-carnitine-binding component of the CbcWV importer, so membership of this NCBIfam family does not fix choline as the ligand.

document.description: BetC (SmCS) is the choline sulfatase of the Sinorhizobium meliloti betICBA operon, a class I (formylglycine-dependent) sulfatase of the alkaline phosphatase superfamily that hydrolyzes choline-O-sulfate to choline and inorganic sulfate. Genetics show that it is required for choline sulfatase activity, and the choline it releases is oxidized by BetA and BetB to the osmoprotectant glycine betaine; choline-O-sulfate can also serve as a sole carbon, nitrogen and sulfur source through the bet locus. The purified enzyme is highly efficient with choline-O-sulfate, hydrolyzes 4-nitrophenyl sulfate far more slowly and shows promiscuous phosphoesterase activity. Its crystal structure shows a buried active site in which a formylglycine nucleophile derived from Cys54, a divalent metal ion and Glu386 (which recognizes the quaternary ammonium group) bind the substrate.

review.summary: Cytoplasmic location is consistent with intracellular hydrolysis of imported choline-O-sulfate and is retained as non-core.
review.reason: TreeGrafter places this protein in the PTHR45953 sulfatase tree and transfers a cytoplasmic location. The choline released by BetC is oxidized by the cytoplasmic BetA/BetB enzymes of the same operon, and choline-O-sulfate is metabolized intracellularly into glycine betaine, which fits a cytoplasmic enzyme. No localization assay exists for this protein, and the location is ancillary to its catalytic role.

proposed_new_terms.proposed_definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of choline-O-sulfate (choline sulfate), typically by hydrolysis of its sulfate ester bond to choline and inorganic sulfate.
proposed_new_terms.justification: BetC hydrolysis of choline-O-sulfate is currently captured only by GO:0042425 choline biosynthetic process (via UniPathway), which describes formation of choline rather than breakdown of an exogenous sulfate ester that S. meliloti uses as a carbon, nitrogen and sulfur source. No GO process term names choline-O-sulfate. Choline-O-sulfate contains sulfur, so GO:0044273 sulfur compound catabolic process ("The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of compounds that contain sulfur") is the natural parent.
